articles.title: I wish Rodri well, but not too well, says Real Madrid boss Mourinho, who lavishes praise on ‘incredible’ Mbappe
articles.summary: Real Madrid open their La Liga season at the weekend and returning boss Jose Mourinho is not concerned that Rodri has joined arch-rivals Barcelona
articles.content:
I wish Rodri well, but not too well, says Real Madrid boss Mourinho, who lavishes praise on ‘incredible’ Mbappe

Real Madrid open their La Liga season at the weekend and returning boss Jose Mourinho is not concerned that Rodri has joined arch-rivals Barcelona

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho is not interested in players who think twice about joining Real Madrid and said that created doubts that Rodri was a good fit at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Spain captain Rodri last night joined Barcelona from Manchester City after a summer in which both La Liga giants pushed for his signature.

The 30-year-old’s decision to join Barca has been viewed as a victory in Catalonia but Mourinho hinted he would never want a player if he wasn’t desperate to join Madrid.

He told El Chiringuito: “Rodrigo had doubts, he hesitated… and Rodrigo’s doubts created doubts for me. He’s an extraordinary player and he behaved impeccably with us, so I have nothing negative to say. But Real Madrid is on a level where you can’t have players who need to think twice about it. You contact the player and he asks you: ‘When do I have to be there?’ That’s the idea.

“Rodrigo was very good with us and I wish him well. Not too well, obviously. But I wish him well.”

Table of Contents

Vinicius has ‘fallen in love’ with Real Madrid – Mourinho

Bar missing out on Rodri, Madrid have had a good couple of months, bringing in several new players, including record-signing Yan Diomande, as well as persuading Vinicius Jr to sign a long-term contract after a lengthy stand-off.

“Obviously I spoke to him, but Vinicius has fallen in love with Real Madrid,” said Mourinho, who takes charge of his first league game of his second spell against Espanyol on Saturday.

“The only thing I told him was: ‘Vini, where do you want to go? You’ve only been in Brazil and you only know Real Madrid… You only understand Real Madrid when you leave. When you leave… that’s when you realise what Real Madrid is. Don’t leave. It’s not worth it.’

“I think what he has felt in terms of the group’s growth, the way we’ve been working and developing, has given him a very important feeling. Vinicius is a machine – it’s a pleasure to watch him work. We have a lot of quality.”

The Brazilian continues to receive abuse from opposing fans – he has been targeted once again in pre-season – and Mourinho believes that while Vinicius Jr can do more to provide opposing supporters with less ammunition, he remains perplexed as to why he is always the one singled out.

He added: “They don’t respect him. In stadiums… I agree with you, and I’ve spoken to him a little about that too. One thing is celebrating a goal with your own fans and another is celebrating in front of the opposing fans. You can find a little bit of balance there.

“But what sense does it make for an entire stadium to boo one of the best players in the world when you have nothing against him? You go and play a friendly in A Coruña or against Schalke and I don’t think Vinicius has played against Schalke before, or against Depor. Why do you boo him the first time he touches the ball? There has to be some kind of middle ground because watching him play is a privilege.”

Real Madrid striker Mbappe is on a ‘stratospheric level’

Vinicius will be a big player for Madrid this season as they attempt to return to the winners’ circle after two trophyless seasons, as will Kylian Mbappe.

Mbappe, like many others, struggled last season as the club imploded under Xabi Alonso and then Alvaro Arbeloa with a fractured dressing room.

“It’s not for me to judge or analyse what he did last season,” said Mourinho. “It was a strange season, a difficult season for everyone. In the end, it’s always the same story. Arbeloa and Xabi took the blame. I always say that winning or losing comes down to multiple factors.

“I told everyone at Valdebebas that on the first day, not just the players: I don’t accept one person taking all the blame or all the praise. That’s not for me. A lot of people got things wrong last year, not only coaches or players.

“When you ask me about Mbappé, I prefer to think about what Kylian can be now. A guy who could have come back on August 14 but showed up on the 12th already tells me something. The reason he wanted to come back on the 12th is because he wants to play against Schalke in at least decent condition. Then he trains like everyone else, with the same commitment, the same desire to improve and in difficult training sessions.

“Mbappé is incredible. Sometimes he makes me laugh in training. Because he’s too good. He’s on a stratospheric level.”

The Real Madrid players have been impeccable, says Mourinho

Mourinho says he has seen none of the problems that derailed Madrid last season and claims the players’ behaviour has been “impeccable”.

“I’ve found a locker room that is desperate to win,” he said. “I’ve found a locker room that is open to common sense, because all I’ve asked of them from day one is common sense. So far, I haven’t had any situation where I’ve had to be the aggressive leader I can be. They’ve protected me from that version of myself.

“Their behaviour has been impeccable. I’ve told them that what I’m asking for is common sense. Saying they have to arrive an hour before training, not five minutes before, is common sense. That’s modern soccer. You have to arrive early, you have to eat breakfast supervised by the nutritionist, you have to go to the gym every day to prevent injuries… it’s for you. It’s for us. Everything I’ve asked them to do is common sense.”

articles.title: Premier League predictions: Title winners? Top four? Biggest surprise and biggest flop?
articles.summary: The 101 Great Goals writers give their predictions ahead of the new Premier League season
articles.content:
Premier League predictions: Title winners? Top four? Biggest surprise and biggest flop?

The 101 Great Goals writers give their predictions ahead of the new Premier League season

Last Update:

The Premier League is back, baby!

And, as is now customary, the writers at 101 Great Goals offer their predictions, placing their reputations on the line to provide you with plenty of talking points.

So, who wins the league, who is going down and who will walk away with the individual honours?

Table of Contents

Jon Fisher

Who will win the Premier League?

Arsenal: Mikel Arteta provides the stability lacking in the Gunners’ competitors. They could’ve done more to strengthen the squad this summer but they should still retain the trophy.

Which teams will complete the top four?

Manchester City, Liverpool and Aston Villa: City and Liverpool are obvious choices. I think Villa will edge out Chelsea for fourth unless Xabi Alonso can streamline a bloated squad.

Who will go down?

Hull, Fulham and Newcastle: Ipswich have learned from previous mistakes and bought Premier League experience while Coventry ought to be good at home. Fulham have lost their best player in Harry Wilson while Alvaro Arbeloa has no Premier League experience. Newcastle are a mess and could implode.

Top scorer?

Erling Haaland: The obvious choice but the Norwegian may be pushed harder this year by the likes of Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyokeres.

PFA Player of the Year?

Declan Rice: The best player at the title-winning club.

Biggest surprise?

Leeds: Impressive last season with a style of football that suggests they can kick on. In Harry Wilson, Tarik Muharemovic and James Trafford they have recruited well. They are more than capable of challenging for Europe.

Biggest flop?

Matthias Jaissle: To be fair to the German, he has been thrown in at the deep end with Newcastle selling Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon. He will be gone by Christmas.

Nicholas McGee

Who will win the Premier League?

Arsenal: With Manchester City transitioning to a new era under Enzo Maresca, it’s difficult to see any team producing the consistency to rival the Gunners.

Which teams will complete the top four?

Manchester City, Chelsea, Liverpool: I expect Chelsea to make strides under Xabi Alonso, while Liverpool should have enough despite some concerning words from Andoni Iraola about his team’s fitness to start the season.

Who will go down?

Coventry City, Ipswich Town, Hull City: Coventry are best-placed to beat the odds but, even with some worrying signs for more established teams, it’s hard to see anything but all three promoted teams returning to the second tier.

Top scorer?

Erling Haaland: Rinse and repeat. The change in manager is unlikely to have much negative impact on City’s goal machine. Another prolific campaign beckons.

PFA Player of the Year?

Declan Rice: With Bruno Guimaraes coming in to take some of the burden off his shoulders, Rice can be freed up to spearhead the Gunners’ title defence.

Biggest surprise?

Leeds United: Leeds have recruited smartly and, with the improvement they have made in the goalkeeping department, have a team with the ability to challenge for the top half.

Biggest flop?

Manchester United: While the midfield is bolstered, the Red Devils don’t look to have a squad capable of competing on four fronts following a quiet transfer window. The first full season under Michael Carrick will bring a step back.

Cian Cheesbrough

Who will win the Premier League?

Arsenal: I was expecting a City bounceback, but that Community Shield defeat and the loss of Rodri has to be taken into account. Arsenal remain the most settled contender and they should defend their title.

Which teams will complete the top four?

Man City, Chelsea, Aston Villa: Man City remain Arsenal’s biggest threat, while I think Chelsea’s easier schedule will see them take third (see Man Utd last season). Despite several changes over the summer, Unai Emery will continue to have Villa competing with the top teams and once again pip Liverpool to fourth.

Who will go down?

Hull, Fulham, Everton: Hull were the last team to secure their place in the PL 2026-27 line-up and they could be the first to leave,, but I do think both Coventry and Ipswich will survive. I can see Fulham struggling under Arbeloa in the post-Marco Silva era, I’m not sure just signing a load of youngsters from Real Madrid’s academy is the smartest move! Newcastle are in for a tough season, but I think Everton may be in trouble and Moyes could be one of the first managers to go.

Top scorer?

Erling Haaland: I’d be shocked if anyone says anything different. Regardless of how City perform, Haaland’s stranglehold on the Golden Boot is unlikely to be challenged.

PFA Player of the Year?

Declan Rice: With Bruno Guimaraes next to him, the England man will have the freedom to showcase his ability even more in another title triumph.

Biggest surprise?

Brentford: Brentford were unlucky to miss out on Europe last season but I think it could work in their favour this time around with so many of their rivals occupied by an increased schedule and workload. I think there’s a chance the Bees could break into the top six.

Biggest flop?

Tottenham: I don’t think spending £200m+ is enough to solve the issues at Spurs and Roberto De Zerbi doesn’t exactly feel like the guy who’ll provide the stability they need. I’m tipping the North Londoners to finish in the bottom half, which, to be fair, is still an improvement on the last two seasons!

articles.title: Brighton sign Canada striker David on loan
articles.summary: Promise David has been prolific in Belgium
articles.content:
Brighton sign Canada striker David on loan

Promise David has been prolific in Belgium

Last Update:

Brighton have signed striker Promise David on loan from Belgian side Union Saint-Gilloise.

The 25-year-old will replace Danny Welbeck after the veteran England forward moved to Premier League rivals Chelsea earlier in the summer.

Brighton sporting director Mike Cave said: “Promise is someone we have been watching for some time, he is an out-and-out striker who possesses outstanding physical attributes and a track record of scoring goals.

“His experience at international level and in European competition will hopefully prove valuable this season.

“At 25, he’s entering his prime playing years and we’re excited to see him continue to develop in our environment.”

David is no relation to fellow Canada forward Jonathan David. In total he made 82 appearances for Royale Union Saint-Gilloise, scoring 41 goals and providing nine assists.

articles.title: Musiala says ‘seizures are a part of life’ after Bayern midfielder collapses again
articles.summary: Germany international says he is fit and well
articles.content:
Musiala says ‘seizures are a part of life’ after Bayern midfielder collapses again

Germany international says he is fit and well

Last Update:

Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala says he is suffering from seizures which “are a part of daily life” after he collapsed again during a friendly win over Heidenheim.

The Germany international went down off the ball just four minutes after coming on as a substitute and was helped by team-mates and officials.

He first collapsed against Leipzig last weekend in extreme heat but there were no temperature concerns on Tuesday.

He was soon back on his feet and has reassured fans on Instagram that he is fit and well.

He said: “First things first – I am doing well!

“I have been diagnosed with temporary, brief, but easily treatable absence seizures caused by a neurological dysfunction.

“These can lead to the kinds of moments seen recently, like against Leipzig or now in Heidenheim.

“I know they look scary at first glance – but for me, they are currently just a part of my daily life. I am receiving the best possible medical care and feel very optimistic. FC Bayern and my inner circle are always by my side and supporting me along the way.”

The 23-year-old played for Germany at the World Cup after a long spell out with a broken leg.

Bayern won the friendly 4-2 with Luis Diaz getting on the scoresheet and England captain Harry Kane playing for the final half hour.

Bayern’s sporting director Max Eberl commented after the game, saying: “We knew and still know about it. When something happens there, like Christian Eriksen’s collapse, or now with Jamal, everyone understands that football is the most beautiful thing in the world and that it’s about something completely different.

“That’s a good sign and gives me a good feeling that we stand together as a society when something like this happens.”

articles.title: Rodri: Barcelona sign Man City star in £65m transfer as Real Madrid miss out on Spain captain
articles.summary: Rodri has completed his transfer from Manchester City to Barca
articles.content:
Rodri: Barcelona sign Man City star in £65m transfer as Real Madrid miss out on Spain captain

Rodri has completed his transfer from Manchester City to Barca

Last Update:

Barcelona have signed Spain captain Rodri from Manchester City for on a four-year deal for a fee which could rise to £65.3million.

Barca failed with offers of £38.5m and £51m for the 30-year-old earlier this month but had a third bid accepted on Sunday, with the midfielder in the final year of his contract at the Premier League club.

The Spain captain scored the winner when City won the Champions League in 2023 and won the Ballon d’Or in the process.

He said: “What we have done together in these years is something both very special and unforgettable.

“These seven years have been incredible. I have cherished every moment of what we achieved together and will always carry Manchester City in my heart.”

Table of Contents

Rodri: Why Barcelona have signed Spain skipper

The 2024 Ballon d’Or winner was named player of the tournament at the World Cup 2026, helping La Roja win the title for the second time.

Following the end of Pep Guardiola’s transformative 10-year reign at City, Rodri’s seven-year spell at the club became increasingly uncertain with his contract approaching expiry.

Barca are renowned for pressing high under Hansi Flick and Rodri’s ability to dictate play through the centre of the pitch should allow the reigning champions to pursue their cavalier style even more effectively as they target a third consecutive Liga title under the German and Champions League glory for the first time since 2015.

One of their key midfielders, Frenkie de Jong, suffered a serious knee injury while representing the Netherlands at the World Cup.

Rodri reportedly wanted a deal last week to avoid having to fly back to Manchester after house-hunting in Catalonia, but the former Atletico Madrid and Villarreal player rejoined his City teammates on Friday to enable City medics to assess his fitness following a minor back operation.

New City head coach Enzo Maresca did not include Rodri in his matchday squad for the 3-0 defeat to Premier League holders Arsenal in the Community Shield in Cardiff on Sunday.

The midfielder says he is fit and raring to go at his new club after a back injury.

He said: “The surgery everyone was talking about was no big deal – it was just an outpatient procedure.

“I’m ready to train with the team, and when the coach thinks it’s time – once I’ve gotten back into the swing of things – I’ll be ready to play. I hope that’s as soon as possible.”

How Madrid may have influenced Barca signing Rodri

Madrid were widely reported to have held unsuccessful initial talks with Rodri in July. Rodri’s agent, Pablo Barquero, told Cadena SER radio in August that the player had informed Madrid he preferred to pursue talks with Barcelona.

Madrid’s interest in Rodri under new head coach Jose Mourinho may have concerned Barca, with some experts suggesting part of the motive for the deal is to stop last season’s runners-up from recruiting one of the finest players in the world.

“At Real Madrid, he would have revolutionised the team and improved the whole club,” former Blancos boss Jorge Valdano told Movistar Plus Deportes (via Marca).

“For me, Rodri is worth €35m (£30m) to Barca for what he would contribute and €40m (£34.2m) to Real Madrid.”

Rodri stats: Manchester City, Spain trophies

In July 2019, City paid Rodri’s £62.6m release clause at Atleti, where he had won the Super Cup in 2018.

Six years later, Rodri was a four-time Premier League champion and had won the 2022/23 Champions League – including the Player of the Season accolade in the competition – and the FA Cup once and EFL Cup twice.

City won the Super Cup and Club World Cup in 2023 and added the FA Cup and EFL Cup again during Rodri’s final season, although they finished second to Arsenal in the top flight.

The Cityzens’ title defence nose-dived in 2024/25 after Rodri suffered a serious knee injury in a home game against the Gunners in September.

The succession of physical issues Rodri has faced over the last three seasons – missing a total of 84 matches for club and country across that period – has coincided with City’s supremacy in England tailing off.

A EURO Under-19 champion in 2015, Rodri has won the 2022/23 Nations League and was the Player of the Tournament as Spain prevailed at EURO 2024.

New club teammate Pau Cubarsi was a distant second to Rodri in open-play passing at the World Cup 2026, finishing 112 behind him.

Fellow Barcelona player Pedri was the only player to attempt more passes in the final third. Here are some of Rodri’s key stats from that campaign.

articles.content:
‘I’m one of you, I always have been’ – Mourinho revels in Madrid reunion at official presentation

Mourinho has signed a contract to the end of the 2028-29 season.

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho described his return to Real Madrid for a second spell in charge as “like coming home”.

Mourinho was officially presented as Madrid’s new coach on Tuesday, his appointment having been announced back in June.

He has signed a contract until June 2029, coming in after a tumultuous 2025-26 season that saw Madrid fail to win a trophy as Xabi Alonso did not manage to live up to expectations, with Alvaro Arbeloa unable to turn things around.

Madrid visit Espanyol for their LaLiga opener on Saturday, and Mourinho was effusive in expressing his delight at returning to the dugout for the club with whom he dethroned Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona in LaLiga in 2011-12.

“This is like coming home,” Mourinho said. “Emotionally, it’s even better than the first time because back then it was about reaching the top of the world, and now it’s more emotional and heartfelt.”

“I’m one of you, I always have been, since the day I got presented in 2010 and the day I left in 2013, I am one of you,” Mourinho said of his message to the Madrid fans.

“I have a fantastic memory of Wembley [at the 2024 Champions League final] when we beat Dortmund, and the affection that was shown to me that day. I really am one of you.”

“You can imagine what it means to me to work for Real Madrid. This is a principle everyone must follow: working for Real Madrid means working for you.

“Words aren’t enough… because it’s like a mission. It’s not about worrying about myself or whether I’ll earn a lot or a little.

“I’m here to help everyone be better: players, staff… To create a culture of hard work, responsibility, ambition, and something I know well, the responsibility and honour of working for Real Madrid. I really like this concept.”

articles.content:
Rooney identifies ‘no-brainer’ signing for Man United after worrying pre-season performance

The United legend believes they should look to North London to address a key issue.

Last Update:

Wayne Rooney labelled Myles Lewis-Skelly as a “no-brainer” signing for Manchester United after conceding to being concerned by Luke Shaw’s pre-season performance against AC Milan.

United have had something of a quiet transfer window, making just two outfield acquisitions ahead of Michael Carrick’s first full season in charge, with Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans coming in to bolster the midfield.

But left-back remains an area of need for United, with that issue coming into focus last weekend as 31-year-old Shaw struggled in a 4-2 defeat to a Milan side led by former Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim.

In the first episode of his new ‘Stick to United’ podcast, United legend Rooney conceded they are unlikely to be able to depend on Shaw, who co-host Mark Goldbridge blamed for all four of Milan’s goals.

And he pointed to Arsenal defender Lewis-Skelly as a potentially astute signing who would address that issue while providing flexibility further up the pitch.

Rooney said: “I thought he [Shaw] had a really good season last season, but he didn’t have the best game against AC Milan

“So, I don’t think you can rely on Luke Shaw to be consistent for the whole season.”

On Lewis-Skelly, he added: “I know we’re hearing that he’s available for not much money. ‘I think it’s an absolute no-brainer.

“I think if you can get a player who can play left-back, he can play centre-midfield. He’s young. He’s got a massive future ahead of him. I think that’s absolute no-brainer if you can bring him in.”

Rooney also revealed his worries around United’s midfield despite the arrivals of Santos and Tielemans, and pointed to one of the latter’s former Aston Villa team-mates as having the right profile for what Carrick needs in his engine room.

“I don’t know who this player is, but I’d like to see some physicality in the middle of the pitch,” Rooney explained. “A big box-to-box midfield player who can break up play, can drive with the ball, can see a pass, but ultimately he’s got to be in that middle of the pitch and you’ve got that physicality.

“I think if you look at Tielemans, you look at [Kobbie] Mainoo, you look at Santos, they’re all small lads, there’s not much pace among the three of them.

“Probably like [Amadou] Onana for Villa, maybe not him, but that profile of player is what United need in the middle.”

articles.title: Fantasy Premier League 2026/27: Five budget options to separate your team from the crowd
articles.summary: Finding those gems that cost little but produce lots is key to a successful 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League season...
articles.content:
Fantasy Premier League 2026/27: Five budget options to separate your team from the crowd

Finding those gems that cost little but produce lots is key to a successful 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League season...

Last Update:

Finding the right budget enablers is essential when building a Fantasy Premier League squad. The cheaper picks may not be players you want to start every week, but they can free up the funds needed for premium assets while still offering genuine routes to points.

This season, there are several low-priced defenders and midfielders with more upside than their price tags suggest. From attacking full-backs and out-of-position options to set-piece specialists and DEFCON magnets, these five picks could help balance your squad without simply becoming passengers on the bench.

Table of Contents

Enzo Le Fée

Price: 6.0m

Ownership: 12.8%

Position: Midfielder

Fixtures: IPS (A), FUL (H), BRE (A)

Enzo Le Fée is back on my FPL radar as one of the standout budget midfielders. He was one of my personal heroes last season after producing five goals, six assists and 13 big chances created, demonstrating multiple routes to points. The Sunderland midfielder also has set-piece responsibilities and appears to be the main penalty taker, while three pre-season goals have provided further encouragement.

I like to think of him as a budget Dominik Szoboszlai: capable of contributing goals, assists and defensive returns. With Ipswich away and Fulham at home in Sunderland’s opening two fixtures, Le Fée looks like an excellent option to start with.

Milan van Ewijk

Price: 4.0m

Ownership: 15.5%

Position: Defender

Fixtures: ARS (A), HUL (H), MCI (A)

Yes, Milan van Ewijk plays for Coventry – but that does not mean he should be ignored as an FPL bargain. At the start of the season, it is impossible to fill your squad with premium players, and Van Ewijk offers an explosive right-back option at a low price.

He registered eight assists and created 46 chances last season, while his long throw provides another route to attacking returns. His DEFCON potential may be limited, so he is not a defender to rely on every week, but he is an excellent bench enabler. The Gameweek 2 home fixture against Hull could also provide an early opportunity to use him.

Trai Hume

Price: 4.5m

Ownership: 4.9%

Position: Defender

Fixtures: IPS (A), FUL (H), BRE (A)

Trai Hume could be one of the most intriguing out-of-position bargains in FPL. Listed as a defender, he has started on Sunderland’s right wing in pre-season and already produced two goals across three matches. That gives him the appeal of an attacking player while retaining the potential for clean-sheet points if Sunderland keep Ipswich out in Gameweek 1.

Hume may not remain in that advanced role all season, especially if Sunderland bring in another winger, but the early signs are extremely encouraging. Rather than chasing points after they arrive, this is a chance to get ahead of the curve.

Leif Davis

Price: 4.0m

Ownership: 4.9%

Position: Defender

Fixtures: SUN (H), MUN (A), LIV (H)

Leif Davis is another budget defender worth considering at just 4.0m. The Ipswich left-back has already underlined his attacking threat in pre-season, scoring twice in the 3-0 win over Rayo Vallecano with two well-timed runs into the box.

Sunderland are the opening opponents, and while Ipswich may not offer reliable clean-sheet potential every week, Davis has the licence to create and attack from wide areas. His delivery, set-piece involvement and previous creative output give him a higher ceiling than most defenders at this price. For managers looking to save money without settling for a purely defensive bench option, Davis is an excellent enabler.

Dan Ballard

Price: 5.0m

Ownership: 4.4%

Position: Defender

Fixtures: IPS (A), FUL (H), BRE (A)

Dan Ballard is a genuine DEFCON monster and one of the standout budget centre-backs in FPL. He returned DEFCON points in around 60% of his starts last season, averaging 11.8 DEFCON per 90 minutes, while his aerial ability also makes him a threat from set-pieces.

Sunderland may struggle to keep clean sheets consistently, which limits Ballard’s ceiling, but his defensive contribution gives him a reliable route to points regardless. Even if Sunderland concede, a DEFCON return can still turn his appearance into a useful four-point score. For a low-cost defender who does not rely solely on clean sheets, Ballard is a very solid option

‘It’s crystal clear’ – Simeone adamant Alvarez will stay at Atletico

For Simeone, the matter is closed.

Last Update:

Julian Alvarez will not play in Atletico Madrid‘s LaLiga opener, but coach Diego Simeone reaffirmed the club’s stance that he will not be joining Barcelona.

Alvarez this summer made his desire to join the LaLiga champions public, revealing during the World Cup that he informed Atletico of his wish to “fulfil his dream”.

However, Atletico have made it clear they are not willing to acquiesce to his request, with CEO Miguel Angel Gil Marin stating the club would reject offers as high as €200million (£171m) for the Argentina forward.

And, because of the strength of Gil’s stance, Simeone believes the matter is now closed.

“Miguel Angel is the club’s owner,” Simeone said ahead of Wednesday’s game with newly promoted Malaga.

“Nothing is more definitive than the club’s owner, it’s crystal clear. It’s like when a judge hands down a ruling: ‘Dismissed’.

“What he said is crystal clear. From a sports perspective, we want to look out for the person, the player, so he can continue to uphold his reputation.

“We don’t see him playing in this game. I hope that over the next four days, he’ll be closer to where we want him to be.”

While Alvarez is set to miss the start of the new league campaign, Simeone is hopeful he will be available to face Villarreal on Sunday.

“I still feel the same way I did the other day in Korea [during Atletico’s pre-season tour]. I handle the sporting side of things,” Simeone added.

“We talked as we always do and I understand that, from a sporting standpoint, he still needs to step it up a bit to be in top form for Sunday.

“He needs more practice. He’s the best player we have and we’re going to try to build a team around him, keeping his level in mind.”

Alvarez has scored 49 goals and provided 17 assists since joining from Manchester City in 2024.

articles.title: Fantasy Premier League 2026/27: Five Common Mistakes to Avoid
articles.summary: It's time to pick your Fantasy Premier League team. Avoid these mistakes and you should be in for a good year.
articles.content:
Fantasy Premier League 2026/27: Five Common Mistakes to Avoid

It's time to pick your Fantasy Premier League team. Avoid these mistakes and you should be in for a good year.

Last Update:

A strong Fantasy Premier League season is not only about finding the right players – it is also about avoiding the decisions that can quietly damage your rank. Chasing last week’s points, making early transfers and overlooking the new DEFCON system are all mistakes that can leave managers playing catch-up.

The key is to stay patient, plan ahead and make decisions based on fixtures, minutes and long-term trends rather than one-off hauls or social-media hype. These five common mistakes are easy to make, particularly in the early weeks, but avoiding them can give your FPL campaign a much stronger foundation.

Table of Contents

Ignoring the New Defensive Meta

For years, the default FPL strategy was simple: target the most attacking full-backs. The defenders playing highest up the pitch, creating chances and arriving in the box were the foundation of almost every squad.

That has changed with the introduction of DEFCON. Defenders now earn two points for reaching 10 combined clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles in a match. An assist is worth only one point more, but a consistent DEFCON return is far more predictable than waiting for an attacking full-back to produce a rare assist.

That does not mean abandoning attacking defenders completely. Instead, prioritise centre-backs with reliable DEFCON hit rates, clean-sheet potential and set-piece threat. Those players offer repeatable returns, plus the chance of an occasional headed goal – giving your defence a much safer and more profitable floor.

Treating Chips Like Panic Buttons

One of the most common FPL mistakes is treating chips as panic buttons. A Wildcard after one bad Gameweek, a Free Hit because you fancy a differential line-up, or a Bench Boost with players unlikely to start can waste huge potential.

Have a rough chip strategy before the season begins and keep reviewing it as fixtures, form and injuries change. This year, you have two sets of chips: one must be used before the Gameweek 19 deadline, with the second available from Gameweek 20 onwards. That makes planning even more important.

Do not simply use a chip because it is available. Look ahead, identify fixture swings, Double and Blank Gameweeks, and build your transfers around those opportunities. We will have full chip-strategy updates throughout the season, but the key is simple: plan ahead, stay flexible and know what you are building towards

Chasing Last Weeks Points

It is tempting: a random centre-back scores from a corner, keeps a clean sheet, hits DEFCON and walks away with a double-digit haul. But one big score does not mean it will happen again. FPL is unpredictable, and chasing isolated returns is one of the fastest ways to waste transfers.

Instead, trust the bigger picture. Assess form over several matches, upcoming fixtures, expected goals and assists, minutes security, player role and tactical match-ups. Ask yourself: would I still want this player if I had not seen last week’s score? If the answer is no, it is probably a trap.

Use trends and underlying data to get ahead of the next haul rather than reacting to the previous one. Good FPL managers plan across a run of fixtures, not one Gameweek, and stay patient when the evidence still supports their picks

Plan Ahead, Stay Flexible

Good FPL managers plan transfers in advance rather than making decisions one Gameweek at a time. Look three to four Gameweeks ahead for fixture swings, likely transfer targets and players you may need to sell. That gives you time to bank free transfers, avoid unnecessary hits and bring players in before their good run begins.

Try not to plan further than six Gameweeks in detail. Injuries, suspensions, rotation, tactical changes and surprise form shifts can quickly make a long-term plan redundant. The ideal approach is to plan firmly for the next two or three Gameweeks, with only a loose idea of what comes next.

Use your plan as a guide, not a rigid rule. Review it after every Gameweek, react to genuine new information and keep enough flexibility to deal with the unexpected.

Don’t Rush Your Transfers

A Gameweek may finish on Sunday, but that does not mean you need to make your transfer on Monday. Time is information in FPL. Waiting gives you the chance to assess midweek matches, training updates, injuries, suspensions and press-conference comments before committing.

The most successful managers typically delay their moves until the final 24 hours before the deadline, with many waiting until the final hours. You can also roll unused free transfers – up to five – so there is no need to force a move every week.

The exception is an urgent price change that would genuinely block a planned transfer, or confirmed news that demands an immediate response. Otherwise, be patient. A late transfer is usually a better-informed transfer.

articles.content:
Memphis Depay agrees new Corinthians deal after writing off £2.9m

Memphis Depay has signed a two-year contract with Corinthians after a stand-off over wages was resolved

Last Update:

Memphis Depay has performed a u-turn and signed a new contract with Corinthians, less than a week after branding the club’s refusal to honour a planned extension as “unacceptable”.

It seemed the Netherlands international’s two-year stint in Brazil was coming to an end after he accused the club of failing to comply with pre-agreed terms over a new deal.

Corinthians admitted they could not afford what they had initially proposed but, following negotiations, a new two-year contract has been agreed with Depay wiling to write off a chunk of money he was owed.

Club president Osmar Stabile said: “Everything’s fine but it was hard work. Obviously, you can’t get an international star done very quickly – it was a lengthy process but everything worked out.

“We had a personal meeting and he managed to reduce the numbers that his team couldn’t achieve. We did what was best for Corinthians, especially in financial terms.”

Table of Contents

Corinthians chief received threats after initial deal with Depay broke down

Former Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and Manchester United forward Depay has scored 20 goals in 79 appearances for Corinthians, helping them win the Copa do Brasil and the Supercopa do Brasil.

According to ESPN Brasil, he has waived around £2.9million to stay with the Sao Paulo club.

“[Depay] reduced it significantly,” added Stabile. “I don’t want to discuss numbers but he made a considerable reduction because of the circumstances, because of his desire to stay, and because Corinthians needed to find a way to pay. I believe we can afford this contract.”

The deal is a major relief for Stabile, who received threats from fans angry that their star man may be forced to leave.

“We suffered the consequences, they leaked my phone, they leaked my daughters’ phones, they invaded my bank accounts, my daughters’, my wife’s,” he said. “It was a difficult situation, no-one deserves a situation like this. There were people showing knives, people showing revolvers. We are now taking the necessary measures. We know that there are a lot of bandits involved, sending WhatsApps to my family. I don’t wish that on anyone.”

Depay performs u-turn to stay at Corinthians

It is quite the about-turn from Depay, who last week outlined his frustration at Corinthians’ stance and vowed to take action.

He wrote on social media: “This renewal was explicitly agreed upon by the president as well as the sporting, legal and financial department. Some people decided however to breach this engagement.

“I didn’t want this situation and always respected the club throughout the process, but now I am forced to react strongly in order to preserve my interests.

“In the upcoming days I will speak publicly but rest assured that I will not leave this unacceptable behaviour unsanctioned.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Newcastle complete signing of Dedic
articles.summary: Newcastle have made their sixth summer signing by bringing in full-back Amar Dedic from Benfica
articles.content:
BREAKING: Newcastle complete signing of Dedic

Newcastle have made their sixth summer signing by bringing in full-back Amar Dedic from Benfica

Last Update:

Newcastle have signed full-back Amar Dedic from Benfica for a fee in the region of £29.5million.

Dedic is predominantly a right-back, although he can also operate on the left, and will provide competition for the injury prone Tino Livramento, with Kieran Trippier having joined Wolves.

The 24-year-old has signed a five-year deal at St James’ Park and is excited at the opportunity to reunite with Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle after working with him at FC Liefering and RB Salzburg.

He told the club’s official website: “It’s a special feeling and a really big honour for me to join Newcastle United. I’m really happy to be here and can’t wait to start playing for the club and the amazing fans.

“Working with Matthias again was a big factor for me. We know each other well, he knows what I can bring on the pitch and I’m really happy to be playing for him again.

“Playing Premier League football at St James’ Park is going to be really special. Every game feels like a big occasion, with an amazing atmosphere. I’m really excited to get started.”

Table of Contents

Dedic will bring quality to Newcastle – Jaissle

Dedic is a Bosnia and Herzegovina international with 31 caps to his name, including three at the 2026 World Cup.

Jaissle said: “I’m really happy to add Amar to our squad. He’s a player who I know really well, having worked with him from a young age in Austria and followed his career since.

“He will bring both defensive and attacking qualities to our squad, which suits the style of football that we want to play. He’s athletic, aggressive and technically very good, but also has a lot of potential to develop further.

“Amar is still young but already has a lot of valuable experience – he’s played in the Champions League and the World Cup, as well as representing huge clubs in Austria, France and Portugal. I’m really looking forward to working with him again.”

Dedic deal is another example of Newcastle transfer policy

Newcastle have not had an easy summer, losing Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, with all three pushing to leave Tyneside.

In their stead, they have recruited a younger profile of player and sporting director Ross Wilson believes Dedic is a good example of the direction the club is moving in.

He said: “I’m delighted to welcome Amar to Newcastle United. He’s a player Matthias knows really well and one we all think very highly of – we see him as a player who strengthens our squad straightaway, capable of performing on the right and on the left.

“He’s shown his level at Salzburg and Benfica as a modern full-back who has the ability to contribute at both ends of the pitch. He’s incredibly hungry to prove himself here at Newcastle United and in the Premier League.”

articles.title: Fantasy Premier League 2026/27: Five key tips to help you succeed
articles.summary: With the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League season just around the corner, here are some fundamental principles to help you steal a march on your rivals...
articles.content:
Fantasy Premier League 2026/27: Five key tips to help you succeed

With the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League season just around the corner, here are some fundamental principles to help you steal a march on your rivals...

Last Update:

A successful Fantasy Premier League season is not achieved in Gameweek 1, but the right decisions early on can put you in a strong position for the months ahead. From building a balanced squad and choosing dependable captaincy options to understanding the growing importance of DEFCON and planning your chips, small margins can make a huge difference.

These five early-season tips are designed to help you avoid chasing points, protect your rank and give your team the best possible foundation. Whether you are a seasoned manager or starting fresh this year, getting the basics right now can pay off across all 38 Gameweeks.

Table of Contents

Make DEFCON Your Foundation

DEFCON defenders should be a major part of your early-season FPL strategy. Attacking full-backs will always have appeal, but attacking returns are less reliable: an assist is worth only one extra point for a defender, whereas consistently reaching the DEFCON threshold earns two points through repeatable defensive actions.

Defenders hit DEFCON by collecting 10 clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles in a match. That creates a dependable floor even when their team concedes, while set-piece threat still offers the potential for the occasional goal. Prioritise centre-backs and defensive-minded players with a strong DEFCON hit rate, some clean-sheet potential and aerial threat from corners. That combination is far more sustainable than chasing attacking returns alone.

Build a Balanced Gameweek 1 Team

There is no such thing as a perfect FPL draft. Some managers will go heavy on premiums such as Erling Haaland, Bruno Fernandes, Bakayo Saka and Gabriel, while others will spread the budget across strong mid-priced options like Joao Pedro, Byran Mbeumo, Antoine Semenyo and Florian Wirtz.

The important thing is choosing a structure that works for you. Target nailed starters with favourable early fixtures, prioritise players who regularly complete 90 minutes, and give extra weight to penalty takers. A balanced squad also gives you flexibility: you can react to early price changes, emerging bandwagons and unexpected injuries without needing to take hits. Avoid overloading your bench with expensive players, but make sure every starter has a clear route to points.

Don’t Get Too Clever

It is tempting to chase the perfect Gameweek 1 differential. A 5.5m midfielder scoring 12 points at 1.2% ownership looks brilliant – but early in the season, prioritising reliable players is usually the smarter move.

Start with assets you trust to play 90 minutes, take penalties, have favourable fixtures and offer proven routes to points. One low-owned punt can be worthwhile, but filling your squad with risks can leave you chasing from the very first Gameweek if the popular picks return.

FPL is a marathon, not a sprint. There are 38 Gameweeks to gain ground, so begin with a solid base and take calculated risks once form, line-ups and team roles become clearer.

Keep The Armband Simple

There is nobody who enjoys a differential captain more than me, but in the opening Gameweeks, the smarter approach is usually to keep the armband on the reliable premiums. Haaland and Fernandes should be the main captaincy options early on: they are nailed for minutes, central to their teams’ attacks and offer elite ceilings through goals, assists and penalties.

Haaland was the captain in 59.3 per cent of picks made by last season’s top 50 FPL managers, while Fernandes was the clear second choice. That tells you everything about the value of dependable captaincy.

Do not feel forced to chase a low-owned armband from Gameweek 1. Start safely, protect your rank, and wait until later in the season – when form, fixtures and team roles are clearer – to attack the best differential captaincy opportunities.

Make Your Chips Count

Chip strategy can define your FPL season. Knowing when to use your Wildcard, Bench Boost and Free Hit is often more valuable than chasing one transfer or one differential.

An early Bench Boost is a viable approach this year, with Gameweek 1 or Gameweek 2 both worth considering if your 15 players have secure minutes and favourable fixtures. For the first Wildcard, Gameweeks 4 and 6 look like sensible points to reassess. By then, we should have clarity on minutes, injuries, team shapes and early breakouts, while Gameweek 6 follows an international break and offers extra time to react. Do not force the chip just because you have reached a certain week – but if your draft has multiple problems, it is an ideal reset point.

Keep an eye out for a fuller chip-strategy guide later in the season, especially once fixture swings, blank Gameweeks and Double Gameweeks begin to take shape.

‘Now is the time to talk about it’ – Kane reveals imminent Bayern contract talks

Kane looks set to extend his successful spell with the Bundesliga champions.

Harry Kane has confirmed he is set to open talks with Bayern Munich regarding an extension to his contract.

England captain Kane has enjoyed three hugely prolific seasons with Bayern since his move from Tottenham in 2023.

He has scored 146 goals in 147 games for Die Roten, winning two Bundesliga titles and a DFB-Pokal crown in his time with the club.

The 33-year-old’s contract is set to expire at the end of the coming season and, while Kane insisted both he and the club are calm about the situation, he revealed discussions will begin in the near future.

“I only have one year left on my contract, so now is the time to talk about it,” Kane said, according to AZ.

“We’ll talk about it next week or the week after. Both sides are very relaxed.”

Bayern face Dortmund in the DFL-Supercup on Saturday before opening their Bundesliga campaign against Stuttgart the following Friday.

Rodri arrives in Barcelona to complete ‘dream’ move

The Golden Ball winner made his ambitions with Barca clear.

Last Update:

Rodri labelled his impending move to Barcelona as a “dream” as he arrived in the city to complete the transfer from Manchester City.

The Spain captain is set to make the switch to Camp Nou after City accepted a third bid that could rise to £65.3million.

Rodri had previously been linked with a switch to Real Madrid before having a change of heart and opting to join their arch-rivals.

And, after landing back in Barcelona, the midfielder expressed his delight at electing to sign for the reigning LaLiga champions.

“I am happy to arrive, they have been busy days,” Rodri told reporters “Happy to be here. Playing for Barcelona is a dream.”

While Barcelona have been the dominant force in LaLiga under Hansi Flick, they have not tasted glory in the Champions League since completing the treble under Luis Enrique in 2015.

Rodri scored the winning goal as City beat Inter Milan in the 2023 final, and the World Cup Golden Ball winner underlined his ambition to end Barca’s long wait to win European club football’s most illustrious prize.

“I am looking forward to working with my teammates and giving my best to win it all,” he added.

“We will aim to win the Champions League and everything available to us.”

articles.title: Chelsea chairman Boehly enters talks to sell stake to Clearlake Capital
articles.summary: Significant change could be coming in the boardroom at Stamford Bridge.
articles.content:
Chelsea chairman Boehly enters talks to sell stake to Clearlake Capital

Significant change could be coming in the boardroom at Stamford Bridge.

Last Update:

Chelsea chairman Todd Boehly has reportedly entered talks to sell his stake in the club to majority owner Clearlake Capital.

A report from the Financial Times claims that Boehly, also the co-controlling owner, and Mark Walter have begun discussions regarding the sales of their 12.8 per cent stakes in Chelsea. The potential deal would value the club at over £5billion.

An agreement would resolve the tensions within the club’s ownership group, which took control at Stamford Bridge in 2022.

Boehly, Walter and Clearlake and Hansjorg Wyss purchased Chelsea for £2.5bn in May 2022, with their BlueCo consortium committing to an investment of a further £1.75bn.

The Daily Telegraph reported that Boehly and Walter now value the club at £5bn, with that figure reflected by the valuation of their respective shares.

Private equity firm Clearlake owns a majority 61.5 per cent stake in the club, with the rest split equally between Walter, Boehly and 90-year-old Wyss.

It has previously been claimed that Clearlake and Boehly would be prepared to buy each other out. Additionally, it has also been said that Clearlake would be willing to purchase any of the shares belonging to its consortium partners.

Walter last week agreed to sell the NBA’s Los Angeles Lakers to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger for $12bn (£9.4bn), with that sale coming as he faces scrutiny from the US attorney’s office.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the US attorney’s office and the Securities and Exchange Commission have launched an investigation into how billions in loans extended to firms with links to Walter or his TWG Global holding company ended up on the books of insurance businesses after going through a third entity.

“Mark Walter and TWG have always acted in good faith, and those who have done business with Mark know him as honest and straightforward,” TWG Global said in a statement.

“We are cooperating with authorities, and we are confident these matters will be resolved favourably.”

There has as yet been no indication that the sale of the Lakers is tied to the investigation. Boehly was part of Walter’s deal to take majority control of the Lakers last year, but it has not been disclosed if he retains an interest in the franchise following the sale.

Boehly and Walter, who are also co-owners of MLB’s Los Angeles Dodgers and the WNBA’s Los Angeles Sparks, are thought to be limited to selling their shares to either Clearlake or Wyss due to clauses inserted in the deal to take over Chelsea, which are believed to prevent major shareholders from selling to outside investors in the first 10 years of ownership.

This year is the last of Boehly’s five-year spell as chairman, with the role set to switch to Clearlake next May. Clearlake duo Behdad Eghbali and Jose E Feliciano work alongside Boehly as co-controlling owners, with key decisions requiring approval from all three men.

articles.summary: Andoni Iraola makes his Premier League debut as Liverpool boss on Sunday, but a club legend has raised concerns about his style of play.
articles.content:
‘No top team plays football like that’ – Liverpool legend aims scathing criticism at Reds ahead of Iraola bow

Andoni Iraola makes his Premier League debut as Liverpool boss on Sunday, but a club legend has raised concerns about his style of play.

Last Update:

Jamie Carragher has launched a scathing critique of Liverpool‘s style of play heading into the season under new manager Andoni Iraola, hitting out at the “basketball game” played by the Reds.

Liverpool kick off their season on Sunday when they travel to St James’ Park to face Newcastle United.

Given the upheaval the Magpies have experienced this summer, the Reds will be favourites to emerge victorious on what is likely to be an emotional day, with the game to be preceded by tributes to Newcastle and Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who died last month aged 75.

Still, Carragher sees cause for concerns following the Reds’ pre-season preparations, with Iraola’s side scoring nine goals and conceded nine across their warm-up games.

Iraola was brought in to replace Arne Slot, who was relieved of his duties after two seasons in charge. Slot led Liverpool to the Premier League title in his first campaign, but they dropped off dramatically last term, slumping to a fifth-placed finish amid significant criticism of the style of play under the Dutchman.

Carragher criticises Liverpool’s ‘basketball game’ style

The success Iraola enjoyed in his time at Bournemouth, who finished sixth last term, came in large part because of the intensity with which his team played.

It is that brand of football that will have attracted the Liverpool hierarchy to the Spaniard, but former Reds centre-back Carragher is worried about an overemphasis on attacking players.

“Liverpool will be interesting this season,” Carragher said during an appearance on The Overlap Fan Debate.

“I’m intrigued to see how it goes and what players they’re going to get and how they are going to go about the season.

“Liverpool have too many attacking players on the pitch, they just want to bomb forward. And it’s the same in pre-season at Liverpool this season – it’s just a basketball game. No top team plays football like that. I don’t believe it.”

However, Carragher does not believe the fans will turn on Iraola if his style of play, which is similar to that employed by Jurgen Klopp during his legendary tenure at the club, fails to deliver results.

“One of the reasons why we brought Iraola in at Liverpool, is because he plays ‘Klopp’ football – not because he’s won lots of trophies, not because he’s managed big clubs – because he presses, they’re energetic. That’s the football that we want,” Carragher added.

“We’re almost at the stage at Liverpool now where the players will get the blame – the fans want high energy football, we’ve got a manager who’s brought that in, so if you don’t do it, it’s on you. So, no, it [the scrutiny] won’t be on Iraola.”

Bruno Fernandes: Man United adamant amid Galatasaray speculation

Man United do not want Bruno Fernandes to leave

Last Update:

Manchester United will reject any offer for captain Bruno Fernandes amid renewed speculation regarding his future at Old Trafford.

Midfielder Fernandes’ contract expires at the end of the upcoming season, though the deal contains an option for an additional year, and he has recently been linked with several European clubs.

Serie A clubs Juventus and AC Milan have both been credited with an interest in his services, along with Turkish champions Galatasaray.

Galatasaray are reportedly preparing to offer €50million (£43m) to United for Fernandes’ services, and are said to be willing to double the Portugal international’s wages.

However, according to multiple reports, United are adamant Fernandes is not for sale.

And, with United returning to the Champions League after experiencing a rejuvenation under Michael Carrick last term, it appears unlikely Fernandes would have any interest in a move away.

United’s long-time talisman was crucial to them surging to a third-place finish in the Premier League in 2025-26.

Fernandes scored nine goals and provided a record 21 assists in the league last season, with his exploits earning him the Premier League Player of the Season award and the Football Writers Association Player of the Year award for 2025-26.

United have been relatively quiet in the transfer market, having signed just two outfield players.

However, with those two moves boosting the midfield with Andrey Santos coming in from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans signing from Aston Villa, Fernandes should have more support as he looks to help the Red Devils build on the performance of last season.

Carrick’s men start their 2026-27 campaign away at newly promoted Hull City on Saturday.

articles.summary: Rodri is expected to complete his move to Barcelona this week after snubbing interest from Real Madrid. And one former Madrid chief believes it is a tactical move from the Catalan giants...
articles.content:
Barcelona are only signing Rodri to prevent Real Madrid getting stronger – Valdano

Rodri is expected to complete his move to Barcelona this week after snubbing interest from Real Madrid. And one former Madrid chief believes it is a tactical move from the Catalan giants...

Last Update:

Jorge Valdano believes Barcelona have targeted Rodri because they were aware of the transformational effect he could have had at Real Madrid.

The Spain captain is set to complete a move to Camp Nou this week after Manchester City accepted a third bid for Rodri last night that could rise to £65.3million.

Rodri had previously been linked with a switch to Madrid before having a change of heart and opting to join their arch-rivals.

Barca’s interest came as a surprise and Valdano, who was Madrid’s sporting director between 2000 and 2005 and then director general from 2009 to 2011, thinks it is a tactical move designed to keep the 30-year-old from having a major impact at the Santiago Bernabeu.

The former Argentina striker told Movistar Plus Deportes: “For me, Rodri is worth €35m to Barca for what he would contribute and €40m to Real Madrid.

“It seems to me that he is a strategic signing for Barcelona.

“He’s not going to influence Barcelona’s game that much, although he will put the stamp on everything that Hansi Flick proposes.”

Table of Contents

Rodri snub a major blow for Mourinho’s Real Madrid

Rodri’s decision to reject a move to the capital is a major blow to Jose Mourinho as he looks to replace the midfield experience lost in recent seasons following the departures of Toni Kroos and Luka Modric.

And Valdano admits the former Atletico Madrid man would have had a major impact.

“At Real Madrid, he would have revolutionised the team and would have improved the whole club,” he added.

“The passes to the strikers would have reached them sooner and he would have picked them out better.

“Rodri is one of those players that doesn’t have much of an impact on the goal, but the whole game. That’s why he’s the best player in the world.”

Rodri to replace De Jong at Barcelona

Rodri will join a Barca squad stacked with players he played alongside as Spain won the World Cup this summer. His arrival at Camp Nou will be timely with Frenkie de Jong currently sidelined.

De Jong suffered a partial tear of a meniscus cruciate ligament during the World Cup with reports suggesting his preferred method of recovery – involving rest and rehabilitation – is at odds with the club’s, who want him to undergo surgery.

The Netherlands international is likely to be sidelined for several months, meaning Rodri will be key to Barca’s hopes of retaining the Liga title for a third successive year.

Flick’s side open their league campaign against Elche on Sunday.

Tottenham to offload goalkeeper Vicario to Juventus

Guglielmo Vicario is poised to leave Tottenham and join Juventus after three years in North London

Last Update:

Juventus have moved on quickly from Emiliano Martinez and are expected to complete a deal today to sign Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario.

Juve called off a move for Martinez on Sunday night after talks with the Argentinian’s club, Aston Villa, and swiftly turned their attention to Vicario.

The Bianconeri have offered a package to Tottenham that would see them take the 29-year-old on a season-long loan with the option to make it permanent next summer.

Vicario will fly to Turin today to undergo a medical and complete the paperwork.

Vicario lost his way at Tottenham

It will bring an end to Vicario’s three-year spell in North London that started brightly before fading.

The former Empoli number one was brought in to replace Hugo Lloris and was the first-choice in his first two seasons, helping Spurs win the 2024/25 Europa League crown by keeping a clean sheet in the final win over Manchester United.

articles.title: Leeds to challenge for the top four, Chelsea to miss out on Europe again and Newcastle to go down: 10 outlandish Premier League predictions
articles.summary: Chelsea to miss out on Europe, Leeds to challenge the elite and Hull to suffer an ignominious relegation. Here, we list our surprise predictions for the 2026/27 Premier League season
articles.content:
Leeds to challenge for the top four, Chelsea to miss out on Europe again and Newcastle to go down: 10 outlandish Premier League predictions

Chelsea to miss out on Europe, Leeds to challenge the elite and Hull to suffer an ignominious relegation. Here, we list our surprise predictions for the 2026/27 Premier League season

Last Update:

Last season’s Premier League threw up plenty of surprises.

Who thought Chelsea, fresh from being crowned world champions, would finish outside the European spots and burn through two full-time managers?

Who thought Sunderland, who clinched a spot in the top flight after edging out Sheffield United in the play-offs, would finish seventh and qualify for the Europa League?

Who thought Alexander Isak, the most expensive signing in British football history, would end his first season at Liverpool with three Premier League goals?

You get the gist.

Here are our surprising predictions for the 2026/27 campaign…

Table of Contents

1. Leeds challenge for a Champions League spot

Daniel Farke’s well-documented tactical tweak at Manchester City in November transformed Leeds’ fortunes and the West Yorkshiremen looked very comfortable in the Premier League thereafter. They suffered just four league defeats in 2026 and also reached the FA Cup semi-finals. The signings of Harry Wilson, Tarik Muharemovic and James Trafford will further improve a good squad and with so many of the established challengers starting afresh under new managers, this opens the door for a memorable season at Elland Road.

2. Matthias Jaissle sacked by Christmas and Newcastle go down

Newcastle have a fortnight to sign some quality before the transfer window closes. If they continue to muddle along – being rejected by a player as distinctly average as Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg is a major red flag –  then they are in serious danger. The departures of Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Bruno Guimaraes leave a gaping hole and while the replacements may be talented, they have no experience of the rigours of the Premier League. New boss Jaissle has an almost impossible job unless his squad is bolstered.

3. Coventry and Ipswich stay up

Sunderland and Leeds provided the blueprint last season on how to survive as a newly promoted club. Ipswich have been active in the transfer market – and appear to have learned the lessons from their last top-flight stint. Gone are the punts on good Championship players and, instead, they have signed the likes of Saka Lukic, Issa Diop and Florentino Luis, all of whom have top-flight experience. Chuck in the £24m signing of Toulouse striker Emersonn and you can see why optimism is high in Suffolk. Coventry start from a stronger base having won the Championship last season and they have done well to re-sign goalkeeper Carl Rushworth on a permanent basis. Energetic midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi could prove a very shrewd acquisition.

4. Hull win fewer points than Wolves did last season

You can debate whether this is actually a surprising prediction. Hull did wonderfully well to clinch promotion last season but their summer business merely lends weight to the expectation they will make a swift return. The likes of Matt Target and Jack Butland weren’t good enough on their last stints in the Premier League while Konstantinos Tzolakis and Jens-Hjerto-Dahl are unknown quantities. Wolves claimed 20 points in a miserable 2025/26 season that seemed doomed from the outset. This could be a similar tale of woe.

5. Chelsea fail to make Europe again

Xabi Alonso has been brought in to right the wrongs of last season but he first has to contend with a hugely bloated squad that needs serious work. The Blues have 41 senior players on their books with the possibility of more arriving. The signings of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck also point to an alarmingly complacent atmosphere in a dressing room populated by young players on hugely lucrative long-term contracts. It appears a mess and it may take Alonso a couple of years to get them back on the right track. Whether he’s afforded that amount of time is another question altogether.

6. Viktor Gyokeres beats Erling Haaland to the Golden Boot

Gyokeres scored 14 league goals in his first season at the Emirates despite regularly looking short of confidence. But, following Arsenal’s title success, the Swede can break free of the shackles and sparkle this year. Haaland comes into a Premier League campaign without Pep Guardiola as boss for the first time. He may also need a little longer to get up to speed after a lengthy post-World Cup break. Enzo Maresca is renown for his patient build-up which may mean fewer chances for Haaland to put away.

7.  Pierre Sage is the first Premier League manager to be sacked

Sage worked wonders at Lens last season but will find the Premier League a different beast. At some point Palace’s inability to keep hold of their best players will come back to bite. Maxence Lacroix is the latest man to leave Selhurst Park, leaving a squad that already appears short of quality. If majority owner Woody Johnson runs the Eagles like he does the New York Jets then it won’t take long for a change to be made.

8. Isak scores fewer than 10 Premier League goals

The Sweden international has struggled for fitness since moving to Merseyside. And it is unlikely he would have welcomed the arrival of new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola. Iraola’s high-energy, high-press game may have suited Isak at Newcastle but his recent injury problems mean he is susceptible to a relapse. Expect plenty of niggles and little rhythm for a player who needs to convince Reds fans he is worth the huge outlay.

9. Benjamin Sesko scores more than 20 Premier League goals

Sesko flitted in and out during his first year at Manchester United but still finished the season as joint top-scorer with 11 league goals. The Slovenian should assume the mantle of first-choice number nine and repeat his prolific numbers at both RB Leipzig and Salzburg. With creative genius Bruno Fernandes operating behind him, this should be a big year for Sesko as he looks to justify his hefty price tag.

10. Enzo Fernandez receives four or more red cards

The combative Argentina midfielder reportedly wants out of Chelsea but with no takers at present he will be forced to stay. His antics during the World Cup, when he was a key antagoniser in Argentina’s last-four win over England before being dismissed in the final defeat to Spain, will mean he is a marked man when the Premier League resumes. His frustration at not getting a move, and being the focus of fans’ fury, will manifest itself in an ill-disciplined campaign.

articles.summary: Highlights and reaction from Premier League pre-season matches
articles.content:
Premier League pre season matches: Reports, results, goals

Highlights and reaction from Premier League pre-season matches

Last Update:

Liverpool, Tottenham, Newcastle and Nottingham Forest were in action as Premier League teams continued their 2026/27 pre-season games on Sunday.

The Magpies faced Strasbourg at home and the Reds took on Como at Anfield, while Forest encountered Brest at the City Ground.

Spurs played a training-ground match against Hoffenheim, having beaten the German club 3-0 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday.

Take a look at the latest pre-season action, including highlights and team selections.

Table of Contents

Tottenham vs Hoffenheim: Maddison returns in draw

James Maddison made a swift and unwanted impact on the Tottenham midfielder’s first appearance in almost a year following a serious knee injury.

The former England international lost possession to Hoffenheim’s Leon Avdullahu and conceded a penalty in his attempt to retrieve the ball.

Adam Hlozek, who curled a shot against the crossbar before Spurs went ahead in the game a day earlier, converted from the spot but Ben Davies swiftly replied by heading in £85 million signing Mateus Fernandes’ cross.

Luca Williams-Barnett gave Spurs a half-time lead when the 17-year-old curled in to turn the scoreline around, only for Valentin Gendrey’s volley to earn Hoffenheim a 2-2 draw, although Kevin Danso hit the bar from Williams-Barnett’s cross.

Tottenham team: Brandon Austin, Tye Hall, Kevin Danso, Ben Davies, Souza (Harry Byrne 69), Mateus Fernandes, Pape Matar Sarr (Jamie Donley 87), Rodrigo Bentancur, Luca Williams-Barnett (Tyrese Hall 87), James Maddison (Reiss Elliott-Parris 46), Damola Ajayi (Miracle Adewole 69)

Newcastle vs Strasbourg: Magpies lose on penalties

Newcastle lost at home to Leverkusen on Saturday and Matthias Jaissle’s new team were back at St James’ Park to face Ligue 1 club Strasbourg, going ahead when William Osula struck from Jacob Murphy’s cross in the 38th minute.

Gessime Yassine fired the second-half equaliser past Ewen Jaouen, who was making his home debut alongside Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure in the 1-1 draw.

Yassine also hit the crossbar before the shootout ensured, Newcastle missing three times as Strasbourg scooped the VisitMalta Weekender trophy.

Newcastle team: Ewen Jaouen, Fabian Schar (Miodrag Pivas 46), Trevan Sanusi, Henry Johnson, Aladji Bamba, William Osula, Bazoumana Toure, Jacob Murphy (Sean Neave 75), Joe Willock (Rory Finneran 87), Dan Burn, (Henry Johnson 46), Dylan Charlton, Jacob Ramsey, Leo Shahar

Nottingham Forest vs Brest: Wood, Netz goals

Forest named a markedly different team from their late win over Leverkusen on Wednesday and went ahead when Chris Wood converted a penalty after Luca Netz was fouled by Mama Balde.

February signing Netz completed the scoring in the 2-0 win by slotting in before half-time from Nicolas Dominguez’s pass.

Callum Hudson-Odoi continued his comeback from injury for Forest, who gave a debut to goalkeeper Steven Benda at half-time.

Forest team: John Victor, Zach Abbott, Jair Cunha, Morato, Eric da Silva Moreira, Xaver Schlager, Nicolas Dominguez, Luca Netz, Callum Hudson-Odoi, Arnaud Kalimuendo, Chris Wood

Liverpool vs Como: Gakpo, Jacquet score

First-half goals by Cody Gakpo and Jeremy Jacquet gave Liverpool a 2-0 home win over fellow Champions League qualifiers Como.

You can read our report from Liverpool vs Como.

The season starts with reigning champions Arsenal hosting promoted Coventry City on Friday. Here are the key details on the first set of fixtures.

articles.title: Maresca claims ‘all teams’ need Rodri: ‘We are going to do something’
articles.summary: Man City midfielder Rodri is on the verge of joining Barcelona
articles.content:
Maresca claims ‘all teams’ need Rodri: ‘We are going to do something’

Man City midfielder Rodri is on the verge of joining Barcelona

Last Update:

Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca says there are “things we need to do” before the end of the transfer window as Barcelona close in on a deal for hugely influential midfielder Rodri.

Barca failed with offers of £38.5m and £51m for the Spain international but were widely reported to have had a bid accepted on Sunday, with the Guardian putting the Spanish side’s successful offer at £65.4m.

“Rodri’s a player who has just won the World Cup and the [2024] Ballon d’Or,” Maresca said after his first competitive match in charge ended in a 3-0 defeat to Arsenal in the Community Shield in Cardiff.

“He’s a top player; all the teams need a player like Rodri. We are quite clear with what we need to do and, for sure, we are going to do something before the transfer window closes. It’s not because we lost.”

Table of Contents

Rodri transfer: Man City defeat ‘not about’ star

Critics called the performance against the reigning Premier League champions a concerning start to the season for City, who are operating without their transformative manager of modern times, Pep Guardiola, for the first time in 10 years.

Maresca assessed new £116 million signing Elliot Anderson’s display as “quite good” and suggested fellow midfielder Mateo Kovacic had played well, although the scoreline was not harsh on a City side who fell behind after 23 seconds.

“We can find many things after this kind of defeat – we just need to analyse it in the right way,” said Maresca. “It’s not about if we miss Rodri or not.”

Rodri returned to training on Friday but is in the final year of his contract. The Guardian also said City are striking a deal with Lille for 18-year-old Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

When does the summer transfer window 2026 close?

The window opened on Monday June 15 and will shut on Tuesday September 1.

After that, every Premier League club can register a squad of up to 25 players, 17 of whom are allowed to be non-Home Grown Players.

A Home Grown Player has been registered with any club affiliated to the English or Welsh Football Association for three entire seasons or 36 months across their career before his 21st birthday, or the end of the season during which they turn 21.

Under-21 players do not count towards the 25-man limit.

What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day?

The deadline is 23:00 BST in the Premier League, but clubs can have an extra two hours to file the remaining documentation if they submit a deal sheet confirming that an agreement has been reached.

The deal sheet must arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes.

For international transfers, clubs also have to comply with the FIFA Transfer Matching System deadline of midnight.

Man City team vs Arsenal

Rodri and winger Savinho were thought to have missed out through injury for City. Erling Haaland had a quiet game in attack, with playmaker Jack Grealish among the substitutes.

Manchester City starting XI: Gianluigi Donnarumma, Abdukodir Khusanov, Ruben Dias, Josko Gvardiol, Nico O’Reilly, Mateo Kovacic, Claudio Echeverri, Phil Foden, Antoine Semenyo, Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku

Manchester City substitutes: Geronimo Rulli, Marc Guehi, Omar Marmoush, Rayan Cherki, Nico Gonzalez, Jack Grealish, Rayan Ait-Nouri, Matheus Nunes, Rico Lewis

Maresca’s team play their first match of the Premier League season at home to Bournemouth. Here are the key details.
